key: e:mine health and safety act 29 of 1996
synopsis: South Africa’s Mine Health and Safety Act 29 of 1996 is the governing mining law, administered by the Department of Mineral Resources and Energy, since renamed the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources; its Regulations Chapter 8 covers machinery and Regulation 8.10 covers trackless mobile machinery (TMM) [f15553, f15554]. Regulation 8.10 was promulgated on 27 February 2015, while critical sub-regulations addressing underground machine-to-pedestrian and machine-to-machine risks commenced on 21 December 2022 under Gazette No. 47790, Notice 2908, with no transitional period [f2272, f15555]. These provisions require diesel-powered TMMs to detect and warn automatically and, if a potential collision is not prevented, slow to a safe speed and then brake automatically; the system must also fail to safe without human intervention [f15556, f15557]. The law specifies no detection percentage, detection distance, false-alarm limit or stopping test, so MOSH specifications and independent testing supply numerical requirements; South Africa was the only country the booklet found with such a legal mandate [f15558, f15552]. Whether the regulations’ “diesel powered” wording includes battery-electric mining machines remains unclear [f15559].
